facts: The formalism of Category Cooccurrence Restrictions (CCRs) is summarized.
Two parsing algorithms interpret Category Cooccurrence Restrictions (CCRs).
Category Cooccurrence Restrictions (CCRs) are Boolean conditions.
Category Cooccurrence Restrictions (CCRs) are conditions on the cooccurrence of categories.
The cooccurrence of categories is in local trees.
Category Cooccurrence Restrictions (CCRs) allow the statement of generalizations.
The use of Category Cooccurrence Restrictions (CCRs) leads to syntactic descriptions.
Syntactic descriptions are formulated entirely with restrictive statements.
Conventional algorithms are for the analysis of context free languages.
Conventional algorithms can be adapted to the CCR formalism.
The paper shows how conventional algorithms for the analysis of context free languages can be adapted to the CCR formalism.
Special attention is given to the part of the parser.
The part of the parser checks the fulfillment of logical well-formedness conditions on trees.
entities: formalism of Category Cooccurrence Restrictions ( CCRs )
